recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR-7742 follow-up is needed in core; any future cleanup of duplicate, unreferenced value-set source files should be handled separately.
issue_request: FHIR-7742 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for DSTU1 MedicationAdministration. It said the administration method value set could confuse readers because many values were not appropriate for medications, and the accepted resolution was to fix the link to the correct value set and add SNOMED CT 422096002 Dosing instruction fragment as an exemplar value set.
initial_application: Commit adf4e89f89fd36602f6b6e7520c1025949477424 explicitly included GF#7742 and GF#5990 and added the administration-method exemplar value set binding, changing MedicationAdministrationMethod from unbound to an example binding and adding 422096002 value set content.
additional_context: FHIR-5990 is the same value-set correction family. Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue FHIR-19913 changed the active Dosage.method value set basis from 422096002 to SNOMED CT 736665006; commit 1dcdc4c567b23fc3748c6474ab1688bf53d662e1 applied that to source/datatypes/valueset-administration-method-codes.xml, and combined-branch commit 8f91c3f2e034f4af575f7e03d56ccb242fca7872 already reconciled the remaining examples. Current active source keeps MedicationAdministration.dosage.method bound to the administration-method canonical, while the active datatypes value set filters on 736665006.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reverting the active value set to 422096002 would contradict the later FHIR-19913 decision, and the old source/medicationrequest copy containing 422096002 is not the active current binding source.
